therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: CD20-targeted B-cell depletion combined with DNA alkylation
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: enhanced B-cell lymphocyte elimination in chronic lymphocytic leukemia
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: previously untreated patients with chronic lymphocytic leukemia

results.effect_size: HR 0.57 (95% CI: 0.45-0.72), median PFS 22.4 vs 13.1 months
results.target_engagement_evidence: ofatumumab plasma concentrations achieved therapeutic levels with Cmax 241-285 µg/mL
biomarker_changes: MRD negativity achieved in 26 vs 8 participants (combo vs mono)
IgG decreased by -0.268 vs -0.458 g/L (combo vs mono)
IgM decreased by -0.031 vs -0.398 g/L (combo vs mono)
subgroup_findings: Complete response rate: 27 vs 3 participants (combo vs mono)
Constitutional symptoms improved more in combination arm
safety_signals: Grade 3-4 adverse events: 103 vs 85 participants (combo vs mono)

dose_info.schedule: ofatumumab day 1 q28d, chlorambucil days 1-7 q28d

context.duration: minimum 3 cycles to maximum 12 cycles, median follow-up 28.9 months
context.investigator_commentary: Majority of patients (62%) had been treated with next line therapies, including new highly effective therapies confounding the interpretation of the OS results.

modulation_entries.hypothesis: CD20-targeted B-cell depletion by ofatumumab enhances the anti-leukemic effect of chlorambucil DNA alkylation
modulation_entries.citation: HR 0.57 (95% CI: 0.45–0.72), p = <0.001 for PFS favoring combination
